text:
alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel routing change we started seeing KV prefill OOM spikes on a subset of GPU hosts during warmup. Hit-rate dropped hard from ~78% -> ~45% on the affected pool.
jen: ugh, timeline? which commit rolled? any correlating config changes (batching/quant)?
alex: rolled 2110c3 — it enabled the new fp16-routing + longer minibatch window. No TTL config changes. Batching heuristic now accumulates up to 32ms instead of 8ms for kernels flagged as 'latency-tolerant'.
mike: that batching window jump would increase inflight sequence lengths — bigger KV footprints. Can you paste the OOM logs and a sample /metrics snapshot?
alex: paste below (trimmed):\n```
OOM: gpu-12 host=gpu-prod-3 cause=kv_alloc failed size=1.2GiB free=32MiB
prefill_hit_rate: 0.45
prefill_mean_seq_len: 142
kernel_path: quant-fp16-deepbatch
```
sara: mean_seq_len 142 vs baseline ~48 — that explains memory pressure. But why did hit_rate drop? longer sequences usually increase prefix reuse.
alex: probable causes: 1) new kernel route uses a different key-normalization path (we changed tokenizer postproc to strip trailing \n in routing path) -> some keys diverged. 2) warmup sampler doesn't account for longer minibatches so prefill cohort skewed.
jen: can we validate key-normalization quickly? sample a few keys from cache and compare pre/post router outputs.
mike: quick diff command:\n```bash
kubectl exec -it cache-inspector -- /bin/sh -c "python scripts/sample_keys.py --pool=prod-3 --limit=200 > /tmp/keys_before.txt"\n# run router in canary mode then sample again
```
we should diff and look for whitespace or tokenization differences.
ops-bot: ALERT: OOM spike detected 2026-03-17T14:12:03Z affected_hosts=[gpu-prod-3,gpu-prod-4,gpu-prod-7] severity=warning
sara: interim mitigations: reduce batching window back to 8ms for fp16-routing (config flip), bump GPU cache soft_limit by 15% on affected hosts, and increase short-ttl from 30s -> 60s to give eviction sweep more headroom.
alex: agree. also propose adding probabilistic eviction (p=0.02) for high-frag slots to avoid slab blowouts — and enable keyhash sampling to confirm collisions.
jen: I'll own the config flip + TTL bump. mike can you prepare a quick rollback patch for the kernel route if key diffs show normalization mismatch?
mike: on it. I'll also add a small perf probe that logs per-request kernel_path + computed cache_key to a sampling stream (1/1000) so we can correlate.
sara: add an eval: run the warmup harness with longer minibatches locally but with the old and new tokenizer to reproduce hit-rate delta.
alex: created a tiny canary: routing flag off for 10% traffic. Will monitor hit_rate and OOMs. If hit_rate returns to ~78% we know routing change caused key divergence.
jen: noted. Action items:\n- jen: flip batching window + TTL bump on affected pool (ETA 15min)\n- mike: prepare rollback + sample logger (ETA 1h)\n- sara: run warmup reproduction (ETA 45m)\n- alex: monitor canary and aggregate metrics (ETA immediate)\nThanks :thumbsup:
mike: one more: let's capture fragmentation stats (slab free list sizes) before/after eviction sweep. That will tell if our sweep is too aggressive and causing slab scattering.
alex: adding that to monitor. Will post results in this thread.
ops-bot: NOTE: canary deployed 10% traffic to kernel-route=false at 2026-03-17T14:20:00Z
